Hidden tests start the real add-on server with Blender replaced by an in-process stand-in and every remote service replaced by in-process responses, then send download_polyhaven_asset, download_sketchfab_model and import_generated_asset commands exactly as src/blender_mcp/server.py does.

traps.shape: the published fix's site: an attached-file path from the asset service is joined to the download folder and the parent directory is created before any write; relative .., absolute paths and the directory side effect all have to be refused, before the directory exists
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported route is the one the report leads to; the risk is stopping at the file write and missing that the directory is created first
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (advisory 787); the shapes are the reader's T1 and the fairness risks it recorded

traps.shape: coupled must-keep-working value: legitimate attached-file keys carry subdirectories, and the same loop creates those directories for the glTF importer, so basename-flattening or rejecting any key containing a separator closes the traversal but breaks a valid model import
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the include keys look like ordinary paths, so flattening them reads as a safe, minimal hardening
traps.realistic_because: real upstream behaviour: the parent directory is created precisely so the nested sidecar resolves for the importer

traps.shape: a second integration builds its archive name from the caller-supplied identifier and writes it before the elaborate zip-slip member guard below, so the identifier decides the archive's directory; relative and absolute forms both escape on Linux
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the handler visibly has a zip-slip guard and the archive is described as a temporary file, so the archive's own path reads as safe and out of the advisory's Poly Haven scope
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the identifier-derived archive name predates the advisory, is untouched by the published fix, and is still present at current upstream HEAD

traps.shape: both Hyper3D transports pass a caller-supplied identifier as the temporary file's prefix, which tempfile treats as part of the path; a separator or absolute form puts the downloaded model in a directory the caller chose. The random suffix limits this to creating a file, never replacing a chosen one, which is the reason it reads as harmless
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the identifier only becomes a prefix and tempfile appends a random suffix, so no chosen file can be overwritten; it is also a different integration from the one the report names
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: both prefixes predate the advisory, are untouched by the published fix, and are still present at current upstream HEAD
